reason: The cited evidence (E1) only demonstrates corrosion resistance of an electrospark-deposited HfNbTaTiZr coating on stainless steel in saline solution at room temperature. It provides no data on high-temperature oxidation behavior, oxide scale formation, oxygen barrier properties, or mechanical property retention, leaving all key premises unsupported.
premises: Electrospark deposition can produce an adherent coating from HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The coating will form a dense, slow-growing protective oxide scale in air at 800–1000 °C.
The coating will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing oxidation.
The coating will not degrade the substrate's room- and high-temperature tensile properties.
